# Data Source: stripe_event_destination_v2

A destination for Stripe's events, delivered as thin or snapshot payloads: a webhook endpoint, an Amazon EventBridge partner event source or an Azure Event Grid partner topic.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_event_destination_v2" "billing" {
  id = stripe_event_destination_v2.billing.id
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the v2 event destination to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `amazon_eventbridge` - AWS account and region where Stripe creates the EventBridge partner event source. See [`amazon_eventbridge`](#amazon_eventbridge) below.
* `azure_event_grid` - Azure subscription, resource group, and region where Stripe creates the partner topic. See [`azure_event_grid`](#azure_event_grid) below.
* `created` - The time when the destination was created.
* `description` - An optional user-defined description of the destination's purpose.
* `enabled_events` - The list of event types enabled for delivery to this destination.
* `event_payload` - Whether to deliver as snapshot or thin events. Possible values: `snapshot`, `thin`.
* `events_from` - The account or organization scopes that can supply events. Use this with `enabled_events` to define the subscription. `@self`: Receive events from the account that owns the event destination. `@accounts`: Receive events emitted from other accounts you manage, including your v1 and v2 accounts. `@organization_members`: Receive events from accounts directly linked to the organization. `@organization_members/@accounts`: Receive events from all accounts connected to any platform accounts in the organization.
* `livemode` - Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.
* `metadata` - User-defined key/value data for the destination.
* `name` - A user-defined label for identifying the destination.
* `snapshot_api_version` - For snapshot events only, the Stripe API version used to render event objects; do not provide this for thin events.
* `status` - Whether Stripe currently attempts delivery. Stripe attempts delivery to enabled destinations when their provider configuration is active; disabled destinations do not receive delivery attempts. Possible values: `disabled`, `enabled`.
* `status_details` - Additional lifecycle context for the destination status, when available. See [`status_details`](#status_details) below.
* `type` - The delivery transport. Chosen when the destination is created and cannot be changed by update. Possible values: `amazon_eventbridge`, `azure_event_grid`, `webhook_endpoint`.
* `updated` - The time when the destination object was last updated.
* `webhook_endpoint` - Delivery target for the webhook endpoint. Live mode requires HTTPS; sandbox mode also supports HTTP. See [`webhook_endpoint`](#webhook_endpoint) below.

<a id="amazon_eventbridge"></a>
### `amazon_eventbridge`

The `amazon_eventbridge` attribute supports:

* `aws_account_id` - Your AWS account where Stripe creates the partner event source.
* `aws_event_source_arn` - The ARN of the Stripe-created partner event source in your AWS account.
* `aws_event_source_status` - The AWS-reported lifecycle state of the partner event source. Possible values: `active`, `deleted`, `pending`, `unknown`.
* `aws_region` - The AWS region where Stripe creates the partner event source.

<a id="azure_event_grid"></a>
### `azure_event_grid`

The `azure_event_grid` attribute supports:

* `azure_partner_topic_name` - The name of the Stripe-created partner topic that receives events.
* `azure_partner_topic_status` - The Azure-reported lifecycle state of the partner topic. Possible values: `activated`, `deleted`, `never_activated`, `unknown`.
* `azure_region` - The Azure region where Stripe creates the partner topic.
* `azure_resource_group_name` - The Azure resource group where Stripe creates the partner topic.
* `azure_subscription_id` - The Azure subscription where Stripe creates the partner topic.

<a id="status_details"></a>
### `status_details`

The `status_details` attribute supports:

* `disabled` - Present when the destination was disabled; identifies the cause, time, and provider-side object involved when available. See [`status_details.disabled`](#status_details.disabled) below.

<a id="status_details.disabled"></a>
### `status_details.disabled`

The `status_details.disabled` attribute supports:

* `reason` - Reason event destination has been disabled. Possible values: `no_aws_event_source_exists`, `no_azure_partner_topic_exists`, `user`.

<a id="webhook_endpoint"></a>
### `webhook_endpoint`

The `webhook_endpoint` attribute supports:

* `url` - The URL where Stripe sends matching events. Live mode requires HTTPS; sandbox mode also supports HTTP.
